correctness.rationale: For safe p>=11, multiplicative order p−1=2q shows primitive roots are precisely quadratic nonresidues except -1, the sole order-2 nonresidue. The character class of four consecutive nonresidues has count B_p=[p−10−4chi_p(2)+S_p]/16: reflection t→−3−t exchanges square/non-square patterns since chi_p(-1)=−1; odd character sums vanish, each distinct quadratic pair sum is −1, and correcting the four zeros gives the -10−4chi2 constant. Scaling x=dt maps all prescribed steps to one of two equal sign-class counts; deleting progressions containing -1 gives exactly E_p(d)<=4. Weil’s degree-4 quadratic character sum bound |S_p|<=3sqrt(p) gives B_p>(p−14−3sqrt p)/16>4 for p>=113. For safe p<113 the finite list 5,7,11,23,47,59,83,107 is complete and all x,d were exhaustively checked; min counts 0,0,0,0,1,1,1,4. The universal part follows from the Weil inequality and finite exhaustive cutoff, not extrapolation from higher sample primes.
residual_risks: The exact formula is only for safe p>=11 and relies on q prime and chi(-1)=-1; p=5,7 handled separately.
Does not assert infinitely many safe primes, all primes, higher AP length or a closed elementary form of the quartic sum.

originality.rationale: Jarso–Trudgian proves the four-CONSECUTIVE (unit-difference) primitive-root question and exact exceptions. Carella 2019/2022 Section 15.1 treats any *fixed tuple of distinct offsets* for sufficiently large p with asymptotic error; that does not provide a uniform finite bound simultaneously for every nonzero d in F_p nor the sharp safe-prime threshold 47. This claim strengthens quantification from fixed d to every field step and provides an exact count with an explicit exceptional -1 correction. The unit-step d=1 specialization is already known at the existence level and is not advertised as new.
residual_risks: A uniform character-sum bound specialized to safe primes may have appeared in earlier primitive-root progression papers not indexed by Resultary.
Carella fixed-tuple theorem is a material antecedent; its asymptotics and table must not be misrepresented as no prior knowledge of arbitrary fixed differences.

value.rationale: Uniform existence of four primitive roots at every prescribed nonzero additive step is a natural strengthening of the classic consecutive-primitive-root question. The sharp least safe-prime cutoff, exact dependence on step and a complete certified finite exceptional range are substantive arithmetic facts; not merely a sample count.
residual_risks: No generalization to arbitrary primes; finiteness of safe-prime sequence is unresolved and not addressed.

final_claim: For every safe prime p=2q+1 with q prime, and every prescribed nonzero step d in F_p, there is a four-term primitive-root arithmetic progression x,x+d,x+2d,x+3d when p>=47, a sharp threshold among safe primes. For safe p>=11, count N_p(d)=[p−10−4 chi_p(2)+S_p]/16−E_p(d), S_p=sum_t chi_p(t(t+1)(t+2)(t+3)), E_p(d) is the explicit sum of 4 tests for a progression containing -1. Exact exceptional step counts are given for all eight safe primes below 113.
